value: In the pre-meal condition (fasted state), significant increased activation for high-calorie versus non-food cues was observed in the orbitofrontal cortex and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, while decreased activation was observed in the posterior cingulate, parahippocampal gyrus, insula, precuneus, and fusiform gyrus.

Activation in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex was significantly higher in Class III compared with Class I/II obesity, whereas activation in the insula was significantly lower in Class I/II compared with Class III obesity.

value: In the post-meal condition (fed state), significant increased activation for high-calorie versus non-food cues was observed in the precuneus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, and medial frontal gyrus, while decreased activation was observed in the precuneus, posterior cingulate, putamen, parahippocampal gyrus, and fusiform gyrus.
In both Class III and Class I/II obesity, activation in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex increased after eating; the difference between groups was not statistically significant.
